newsitem.title: GERMANY: German opposition hails EU ruling on UK work hours.
newsitem.headline: German opposition hails EU ruling on UK work hours.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Tuesday hailed a European Court of Justice decision to reject Britain's challenge to an EU law setting a maximum working week of 48 hours.
"This makes it clear that Britain cannot play a special role in this question," SPD European affairs spokeswoman Heidemarie Wieczorek-Zeul said in a statement.

"The decision by the European Court of Justice on applying minimum social standards in Britain strengthens the rights of British workers and stops countries from undercutting others with looser labour regulation," she said.
She said the SPD had long called for EU legislation to harmonise working conditions in member countries.
"Once it wins the next election, the Labour Party will apply the Social Charter and assure more social security for British workers," she added.
The Luxembourg-based court dealt Britain a blow by rejecting its argument that the law had been improperly adopted as a health and safety measure.

The verdict means European Union states could face a battle in their talks to amend the Union's treaty. British Prime Minister John Major has vowed to block other reforms unless he wins changes to protect Britain from such laws.
